text:
maria: Quick heads-up — ran a perf sweep of the 'route-gate' ROCm branch across MI250 on ROCm-5.4. Seqlen buckets 8/64/256/512. Seeing inconsistent kernel picks and a big latency cliff at seqlen=512. Uploaded raw traces to perf-bot.

perf-bot: Profile artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/route-gate/2026-03-18/gate-mi250-512.tar.zst. Summary: +3.1x dispatch latency @ seqlen=512, KV cache hit-rate unchanged. Flamegraphs in the artifact.

ben: Hmm. Do you have a quick log? sounds like missing specialized kernel variant causing soft-fallback to generic path. That explains 3x.

maria: Attached snippet from runtime log:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] INFO dispatch: looking for kernel=tiling_v3.int8 arch=mi250 seqlen=512
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] WARN dispatch: no match found for tiling_v3.int8 -> trying tiling_v3.fp16
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] WARN dispatch: tiling_v3.fp16 not present for this build -> falling back to generic_attention_kernel
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] INFO exec: using generic_attention_kernel (latency++).
```

maria: So runtime is falling through two levels and hits the generic kernel.

olivia: Is this an autotune DB/backfill gap? We only backfilled int8 autotune rows for mi100 last quarter; MI250 might not have the int8 tiling_v3 entry for seqlen 512.

leo: I can repro locally. Minimal repro command: `./bench --model=gpt-small --device=mi250 --seqlen=512 --quant=int8 --route-table=route-gate` -> see identical fallthrough. Logs show dispatch choosing generic kernel during first forward.

ben: Proposal: change conditional routing policy so that when exact quantized variant is missing, prefer a tiled fp16 variant (if present) before generic. FP16 still better than generic for tiled workloads. We lose some memory/throughput but avoid 3x latency.

maria: Agreed. Two action items: (1) runtime routing policy change (prefer fp16 tiled as secondary fallback), behind a runtime flag; (2) schedule an autotune probe for mi250 seqlen=512 int8 to populate the DB. Also add metric for soft-fallback counts per model+seqlen.

perf-bot: Autotune job scheduled: gate-mi250-512 (probe) -> scheduled 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z.

leo: Draft CL for routing change (local patch):
```diff
- // exact match only
- if (hasKernel(exactKey)) return exactKey;
- // otherwise fall through to generic
+ // prefer tiled fp16 as a secondary fallback when quantized kernel missing
+ if (hasKernel(exactKey)) return exactKey;
+ if (isQuantized(exactKey) && hasKernel(convertToFp16Tiled(exactKey))) return convertToFp16Tiled(exactKey);
+ // final fallback -> generic
```

leo: I'll include a runtime flag `runtime.route_prefer_fp16_on_quant_miss` with default=false for canary.

olivia: Also add a Prometheus counter `runtime_kernel_soft_fallback_total{model, seqlen, reason}` and a 5xx-like alert if fallback_rate > 1% over 5m for production models.

ben: :thumbsup: I'll run the patch through our internal perf harness for MI250 canary. If it drops dispatch latency back near tiled levels, we can flip flag for canary rollout.

maria: Canary plan: roll to a small fraction of traffic behind flag. cc @sre for maintenance window. We'll keep the old behavior for Dedicated customers unless they opt-in.

sre-bot: Canary window reserved: 2026-03-20T04:00:00Z -> 2026-03-20T12:00:00Z. Monitoring hooks: perf-dispatch-latency, kernel-soft-fallback-rate, kvcache-hitrate.

maria: Thanks everyone. Next steps: 1) leo sends CL w/ flag and metric (ETA 3h). 2) ben runs perf harness and posts numbers. 3) perf-bot runs autotune probe and we reconcile DB entries. I'll follow up with postmortem if we see regression on canary.

ben: On it.

leo: CL up in 30m.

olivia: I'll file a short doc in /docs/autotune/mi250-backfill.md with reasoning and thresholds for future probes.

maria: Perfect. Keeping this thread as the action tracker. :sparkles:
